record.title: Akbari–Khaghanpoor–Moazzeni colorful-path conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, and call a path **colorful** under a proper $\chi(G)$-coloring when its $\chi(G)$ vertices have pairwise distinct colors. **Akbari–Khaghanpoor–Moazzeni's conjecture.** Every connected graph $G$ other than $C_7$ admits a $\chi(G)$-coloring such that every vertex of $G$ is the beginning of a colorful path. This conjecture asks for a coloring that provides a colorful path starting at every vertex; the paper studies this conjecture and proves special cases, while the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Bessy Stéphane and Bousquet Nicolas, “Colorful paths for 3-chromatic graphs”, arXiv:1503.00965 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.00965

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: MSOL recognizability conjecture for 3-connected and general $k$-outerplanar graphs
record.statement: Fix $k$ and consider $k$-outerplanar graphs, with the subclass of 3-connected $k$-outerplanar graphs. A graph property is **recognizable** if it is recognized by a finite-state tree automaton; it is **MSOL-definable** or **CMSOL-definable** if it can be expressed in monadic second-order logic or counting monadic second-order logic, respectively. **The $k$-outerplanar recognizability conjecture.** (i) For 3-connected $k$-outerplanar graphs, recognizability equals MSOL-definability. (ii) For $k$-outerplanar graphs, recognizability equals CMSOL-definability. The paper establishes the corresponding results for bounded-degree $k$-outerplanar graphs and proposes these statements as further cases of Courcelle's conjecture; the conjecture remains open in the stated generality.
record.source_name: Lars Jaffke and Hans L. Bodlaender, “MSOL-Definability Equals Recognizability for Halin Graphs and Bounded Degree k-Outerplanar Graphs”, arXiv:1503.01604 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01604

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: Kleitman–Pinchasi conjecture on bichromatic lines
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ red points and either $n$ or $n-1$ blue points in the Euclidean plane. A **bichromatic line** is a line containing at least one red and one blue point, and $P$ **determines** a line when the line contains at least two points of $P$. **Kleitman–Pinchasi conjecture.** If neither colour class is collinear, then $P$ determines at least $|P|-1$ bichromatic lines.

The conjecture gives a lower bound for bichromatic lines determined by two differently coloured point sets; the paper proves it, in fact under the weaker assumption that $P$ is not collinear or a near-pencil.
record.source_name: Michael S. Payne, “Bichromatic lines in the plane”, arXiv:1503.06281 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06281

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: J170 three-weight code conjecture
record.statement:
Let $m\equiv 2\pmod 4$ with $m\geq 6$, and define

$$
f(x)=x+x^{2^{(m-2)/2}+2^{m-1}}+x^{2^{(m-2)/2}+2^{m-1}+1}\in\operatorname{GF}(2^m)[x],
$$

$$
D_f=\{f(x):x\in\operatorname{GF}(2^m)\}\setminus\{0\}.
$$

**J170 code conjecture.** The binary code ${\mathcal C}_{D_f}$ has parameters

$$
[2^{m-1}-1,\,m,\,2^{m-2}-2^{(m-2)/2}]
$$

and weight enumerator

$$
1+(2^{m-3}+2^{(m-4)/2})z^{2^{m-2}-2^{(m-2)/2}}+(3\cdot2^{m-2}-1)z^{2^{m-2}}+(2^{m-3}-2^{(m-4)/2})z^{2^{m-2}+2^{(m-2)/2}}.
$$

The source also recalls the separate conjecture that $D_f$ is a difference set with parameters $(2^m-1,2^{m-1}-1,2^{m-2}-1)$, attributed to Chapter 4 of Ding's book.
record.source_name: Cunsheng Ding, “Linear Codes from Some 2-Designs”, arXiv:1503.06511 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06511

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: Ding's conjectured difference sets from x(x+1) polynomials
record.statement:
Let $m\geq 4$ and, for $f\in\operatorname{GF}(2^m)[x]$, define

$$
D_f=\{f(x(x+1)):x\in\operatorname{GF}(2^m)\}\setminus\{0\}.
$$

**Ding's second difference-set conjecture.** For the following three polynomials, with the indicated parity conditions,

$$
f(x)=x+x^{2^{(m+1)/2}-1}+x^{2^m-2^{(m+1)/2}+1}\quad(m\text{ odd}),
$$

$$
f(x)=x+x^{(2^m+1)/3}+x^{(2^{m+1}-1)/3}\quad(m\text{ odd}),
$$

$$
f(x)=x+x^{2^{(m+2)/2}-1}+x^{2^m-2^{m/2}+1}\quad(m\text{ even}),
$$

$D_f$ is a difference set in $(\operatorname{GF}(2^m)^*,\times)$ with Singer parameters

$$
(2^m-1,\,2^{m-1}-1,\,2^{m-2}-1).
$$

The claim is another list of conjectured cyclic difference sets attributed in the source to Chapter 4 of Ding's book.
record.source_name: Cunsheng Ding, “Linear Codes from Some 2-Designs”, arXiv:1503.06511 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06511

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: The odd graph Hamiltonicity conjecture
record.statement: For $k\geq 1$, let the **odd graph** $K(2k+1,k)$ be the Kneser graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of $[2k+1]$, with edges between disjoint sets. **Odd graph Hamiltonicity conjecture.** For any $k\geq 1$, except for $k=2$, the odd graph $K(2k+1,k)$ has a Hamilton cycle. The exception $k=2$ is the Petersen graph. The source presents this as a longstanding special case of Kneser graph Hamiltonicity and does not state that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Torsten Mütze and Pascal Su, “Bipartite Kneser graphs are Hamiltonian”, arXiv:1503.09175 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.09175

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: Akiyama–Watanabe–Albertson–Haas conjecture on induced forests in bipartite planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple bipartite planar graph of order $n$. An **induced forest** is a vertex-induced subgraph of $G$ that is a forest.

**Akiyama–Watanabe–Albertson–Haas conjecture.** Every bipartite planar graph of order $n$ admits an induced forest of order at least

$$
\frac{5n}{8}.
$$

This strengthens the general lower-bound problem for planar graphs by imposing bipartiteness and seeking a larger induced forest. The source states the conjecture but gives no resolution; partial lower bounds and related results are discussed.
record.source_name: François Dross, Mickael Montassier and Alexandre Pinlou, “A lower bound on the order of the largest induced forest in planar graphs with high girth”, arXiv:1504.01949 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.01949

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

record.title: Amicability–anti-amicability permutation conjecture for Clifford basis matrices
record.statement: Let $m\geqslant 0$. Consider the $4^m$ canonical basis matrices of the real representation of the Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}_{m,m}$; a pair has disjoint support when the supports of its two matrices are disjoint, and is **amicable** or **anti-amicable** according as the corresponding product is symmetric or skew. **Amicability–anti-amicability permutation conjecture.** There is a permutation $\pi$ of the set of $4^m$ canonical basis matrices that sends every amicable pair with disjoint support to an anti-amicable pair, and vice versa. The conjecture concerns a global symmetry exchanging the two edge types in the restricted amicability/anti-amicability graph; its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: Paul Leopardi, “Twin bent functions, strongly regular Cayley graphs, and Hurwitz-Radon theory”, arXiv:1504.02827 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.02827

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

record.title: Daskalakis–Mehta–Papadimitriou's bounded-cycle-or-undominated-set conjecture
record.statement:
Let a **digraph** be a directed graph, and call a set of vertices **undominated** if no vertex has an arc to every vertex in the set. 

**Daskalakis–Mehta–Papadimitriou's conjecture.** There are integers $k$ and $l$ such that every digraph either has a cycle of length at most $k$ or an undominated set of $l$ vertices.

The conjecture was proposed in connection with constructing well-supported Nash equilibria of small support in bimatrix win-lose games; the authors believed it held with $k=l=3$. It was disproved by the paper from which this statement is taken, so the conjecture is no longer open.
record.source_name: Yogesh Anbalagan, Hao Huang, Shachar Lovett, Sergey Norin, Adrian Vetta and Hehui Wu, “Large Supports are required for Well-Supported Nash Equilibria”, arXiv:1504.03602 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.03602

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Klostermeyer et al.'s self-similarity conjecture for the Pascal rhombus modulo 2
record.statement:
Let $R[n,k]$ denote the entry in row $n$ and column $k$ of the Pascal rhombus, reduced modulo $2$. For $n\ge 1$, consider the triangle whose corners are $[1,0]$, $[2^{n-1},-(2^{n-1}-1)]$, and $[2^{n-1},2^{n-1}-1]$. **Klostermeyer et al.'s self-similarity conjecture.** This triangle is identical to each of the triangles with corners

$$
[2^n+1,-2^n],\quad [2^n+2^{n-1},-(2^n+2^{n-1}-1)],\quad [2^n+2^{n-1},-(2^n-2^{n-1}+1)]
$$

and

$$
[2^n+1,2^n],\quad [2^n+2^{n-1},2^n-2^{n-1}+1],\quad [2^n+2^{n-1},2^n+2^{n-1}-1].
$$

This conjecture predicts a threefold recursive structure in the Pascal rhombus modulo $2$, analogous to the self-similarity of Pascal's triangle modulo $2$ and the Sierpiński gasket; the source gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Paul K. Stockmeyer, “The Pascal Rhombus and the Stealth Configuration”, arXiv:1504.04404 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.04404

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

record.title: Klostermeyer et al.'s row-count formula conjecture for the Pascal rhombus
record.statement:
Let $I_n$ be the number of ones in row $m=2^n$ of the Pascal rhombus, with entries reduced modulo $2$. **Klostermeyer et al.'s row-count formula conjecture.** Then

$$
I_n=\frac{1}{3}\left(2^{n+2}-(-1)^n\right).
$$

The formula predicts the number of odd entries in power-of-two rows and is part of the proposed structural theory of the Pascal rhombus modulo $2$; the source gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Paul K. Stockmeyer, “The Pascal Rhombus and the Stealth Configuration”, arXiv:1504.04404 (2015).
record.references:

record.title: Unimodality of rectangular Narayana numbers
record.statement:
Let $N(n,m;k\mid 1)$ denote the rectangular Narayana numbers, indexed by $0\le k\le (n-1)(m-1)$. The sequence is symmetric about its midpoint. **Rectangular Narayana unimodality conjecture.** If $1\le k\le (n-1)(m-1)/2$, then

$$
N(n,m;k-1\mid 1)\le N(n,m;k\mid 1),
$$

i.e. the sequence $\{N(n,m;k\mid 1)\}_{k=0}^{(n-1)(m-1)}$ is symmetric and unimodal. This asserts unimodality of the rectangular Narayana distribution; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: A. N. Kirillov, “Rigged Configurations and Catalan, Stretched Parabolic Kostka Numbers and Polynomials: Polynomiality, Unimodality and Log-concavity”, arXiv:1505.01542 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01542

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Dehmer–Kraus–Schaumann's minimal dendrimer entropy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a dendrimer on $n$ vertices, with orbit weights $c_i$ satisfying $c_i=c_j$ whenever $i\neq j$. Let $I_{f^3}(D)$ denote the corresponding entropy; the star graph has radius $r=1$ and progressive degree $p=n-2$.

**Dehmer–Kraus–Schaumann's conjecture.** The star graph has the minimal value of $I_{f^3}(D)$.

This is a second conjecture on extremal dendrimer entropy, proposed in the cited work for the stated class of weight sequences. The supplied source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Meiqin Wei, “A survey of recent results in (generalized) graph entropies”, arXiv:1505.04658 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Dehmer–Kraus's two-tailed-comet conjecture for tree entropies
record.statement:
Let $T_{n,d}$ be the family of trees of order $n$ with fixed diameter $d$, and assume $d\ll n$. Let $C_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lceil n/2\rceil}$ denote the two-tailed comet appearing in the claim. The entropies under consideration are $I_{f^2}(G)$ and $I_{f^3}(G)$.

**Dehmer–Kraus's conjecture.** Among all trees $T_{n,d}$ with $d\ll n$, the two-tailed comet

$$
C_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lceil n/2\rceil}
$$

achieves the maximal values of the entropies $I_{f^2}(G)$ and $I_{f^3}(G)$.

The preceding theorem proves a comparison between two-tailed comets and ordinary comets for specified decreasing weight sequences, whereas this conjecture asserts a broader extremal property among all trees in the family. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Meiqin Wei, “A survey of recent results in (generalized) graph entropies”, arXiv:1505.04658 (2015).
record.references:

record.title: Kraus–Dehmer–Schaumann's highly connected minimal-entropy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $I_{f^\sigma}(G)$ denote the entropy associated with the sphere function. A graph is **highly connected** here when it is obtained from the complete graph $K_n$ by removing a small number of edges.

**Kraus–Dehmer–Schaumann's conjecture.** A minimal graph for $I_{f^\sigma}(G)$ is highly connected. In particular, a minimal graph on $n$ vertices has at least $m\geq n/2$ vertices of degree $n-1$.

The conjecture is motivated by computations for graphs on $8$ and $9$ vertices and by the observed structure of minimal graphs. It predicts that extremal graphs for this entropy are close to complete and contain many universal vertices.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Meiqin Wei, “A survey of recent results in (generalized) graph entropies”, arXiv:1505.04658 (2015).

record.title: Stress-free geometric graph conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a geometric graph embedded in $\mathbb R^d$, with edges joining pairs at the diameter distance. Call $G$ **stress-free** if there are no not-all-zero edge weights whose weighted edge vectors sum to zero at every vertex. **Stress-free geometric graph conjecture.** If $G$ is a stress-free geometric graph of diameters in $\mathbb R^d$, then $G$ is $(d+1)$-colorable. The source presents this as the finite case of its transversality conjecture and gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Gil Kalai, “Some old and new problems in combinatorial geometry I: Around Borsuk's problem”, arXiv:1505.04952 (2015).
record.references:

record.title: Castle, Evans and Hyde's conjecture on polyhedral toroidal molecules
record.statement: A **polyhedral** molecule has an underlying graph that is abstractly planar, 3-connected, and simple; a molecule is **toroidal** when its graph embedding on the standard torus does not embed on the sphere. **Castle, Evans and Hyde's conjecture.** All polyhedral toroidal molecules contain a nontrivial knot or a nonsplit link. This conjecture predicts that toroidal embeddings of sufficiently rigid abstractly planar molecular graphs cannot be ravel-like: their nonplanarity must be detected by a knot or a nonsplit link.
record.source_name: Senja Barthel and Dorothy Buck, “Toroidal embeddings of abstractly planar graphs are knotted or linked”, arXiv:1505.05696 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05696

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Conjecture that binary words maximize the number of abelian square factors
record.statement: For a finite word, an **abelian square** is a factor formed by concatenating two anagrammatic words. **Binary-word maximality conjecture.** If a word of length $n$ contains $k$ distinct abelian square factors, then some binary word of length $n$ contains at least $k$ distinct abelian square factors. The paper leaves this as an open question after proving quadratic abelian-square richness for several binary-word classes; it is presented as a conjecture supported by the authors' investigation.
record.source_name: Gabriele Fici and Filippo Mignosi, “Words with the Maximum Number of Abelian Squares”, arXiv:1506.03562 (2015).

record.title: Blondeau et al.'s differential 8-uniformity conjecture for two power functions
record.statement:
Let $n=2m$ with $m$ odd, and let $F_d:x\mapsto x^d$ be a power permutation polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$, where

$$
d=2^m+2^{(m+1)/2}+1
$$

or

$$
d=2^{m+1}+3.
$$

**Blondeau et al.'s conjecture.** For each of these two values of $d$, $F_d$ is differentially $8$-uniform, and all values $0,2,4,6,8$ occur in its differential spectrum. The paper presents this as an open conjecture of Blondeau et al.; the supplied text does not indicate a resolution.
record.source_name: Jingxue Ma, Tao Zhang, Tao Feng and Gennian Ge, “Some new results on permutation polynomials over finite fields”, arXiv:1506.05525 (2016).

record.title: Criterion for nonaccumulation of complex eigenvalues near zero for Pauli operators
record.statement:
Let $V=eta W$ satisfy Assumption (C1), with $Eta
iC\setminusR e^{ik\frac{\pi}{2}}$, $k\inZ$, and $W\in\mathfrak{B}_h(\mathbb{R}^3)$ of definite sign. Here $P_3(b,V)$ denotes the three-dimensional Pauli operator with magnetic field $b$ and potential $V$, and $\Re(V)$ is the real part of the potential.

**Nonaccumulation criterion.** There is no accumulation of complex eigenvalues of $P_3(b,V)$ near zero if and only if $\Re(V)>0$.

The statement proposes a generalization of the preceding result for the specific perturbations considered in the paper. The source presents more general magnetic fields and perturbations of the magnetic field itself as open problems.
